name: Breathwick
subtitle: Box, 4-7-8 & coherent pacing
shortDescription: Follow a glowing 3D orb or lotus that swells as you breathe in and settles as you breathe out. Five guided rhythms, haptics, streaks. Free, works offline.
longDescription:
Breathe with something you can see and feel.

Breathwick is a guided breathing trainer built around a real-time 3D visual. A glass-like orb (or an opening lotus) grows while you breathe in, rests while you hold and softens while you breathe out. Glowing particles drift inward on the in-breath and outward on the out-breath, so you can keep your rhythm with your eyes, your fingertips or both.

### Five Guided Rhythms
- Box breathing, an even four-count square
- 4-7-8 wind-down, with a long out-breath
- Coherent breathing, smooth waves of about five breaths a minute
- Pursed-lip pacing, short in and twice as long out
- Long exhale, gentle in and extended out
- Your own rhythm: set every count from 2 to 12 seconds

### See It, Feel It, Hear It
- Physically based 3D rendering with soft glow, depth and floating particles
- Two visuals (Orb and Lotus) and four colour palettes: Tide, Dawn, Ember, Moss
- Haptics that swell and fade with each breath (on iPhones with a Taptic Engine)
- Optional soft tone that rises and falls with your breath, generated live, no downloads
- Keep your eyes closed and follow the vibration alone

### A Habit That Sticks
- Start in seconds: pick a rhythm, pick 1, 3, 5 or 10 minutes, tap Start
- Daily goal ring, day streaks and a 12-week calendar
- Weekly minutes, time by rhythm and milestone badges
- Optional daily reminder at the time you choose

### Made to Be Read
- A- and A+ text zoom on every screen, up to about 200%, on top of iOS Dynamic Type
- Designed for iPhone and iPad, with a roomy side-by-side layout on iPad

### Private and Offline
- Works fully offline from the first launch
- No account, no sign-up. Your sessions stay on your device
- No health sensors, no HealthKit, no camera, no microphone

### Education Only
Breathwick is for relaxation and general wellness. It is not a medical device and does not diagnose, treat, cure or prevent any condition or give medical advice. If you feel dizzy or uncomfortable, stop and breathe normally.
